title: Skrongle course files
description: Schemas for course.json (the manifest), for placement.json (the placement test), and for one lesson file. See /docs/course-format for the prose reference. Older aliases (level, category, es/en, journey, verb/tense, target_grammar_point, markdown_content, example_es/en) are also accepted by the app but are not listed here.

label.description: Shown as the column / card side heading, e.g. "Español" or "Term".

lang.description: BCP 47 language tag for lang= attributes, or "".

id.description: Course id. Built-in courses: must equal the folder name.

levels.description: True when the units are levels (A1, A2…): a learner opening the course picks the one to start at, and the lessons below it are skipped (not passed). Default false: no picker.

order.description: Built-in courses only: where the course comes among the ready-made ones, lowest first; courses without it come after, in folder order. Means nothing for a course someone made in the app. Anything but a whole number is ignored.

language_features.description: Language features on or off: Listening, Sprint's listening exercises and sentence builds, read-aloud, Numbers by ear, and the translation fields in the lesson editor. Unset: on when terms.lang differs from meanings.lang. The editor's gear sets it.

chars.description: Single characters offered as tap-to-insert buttons.

calendar.description: Weekday and month names in the course's language, for the Date Dash game.

days.description: The seven weekday names, Monday first.

months.description: The twelve month names, January first.

format.description: How a full date is written; {day} and {month} are required, {d} and {year} optional.

note_names.description: How notes are named on screen: letters (C D E, F♯, B♭), solfege (Do Re Mi, Fa♯) or german (C D E, Fis, H for B, B for B flat). In a multiple-choice question with abc, an option written as an ABC note (A, ^F, _B, c) is shown in these names.

icon.description: An emoji or short glyph (1 to 4 characters, no markup).

example_meaning.description: The example in the meaning language; shown as a hint on the example.

question_id.description: Unique across the whole course; prefix with the lesson id.

options.description: multiple-choice: 2 or more, must contain correct_answer. clock: times (H:MM) to pick from; the clock shows correct_answer.

correct_answer.description: true-false: "true" or "false". numeric: a number (3/4, 1.5, 2^10), values separated by ; for an any-order list. expression: an algebraic expression such as 2x^2 - 3x + 1. fill-bar: tiles that fill the gap, separated by spaces; may be left out unless exact. chord-spell: the chord's 3 or 4 notes in ABC, separated by spaces, such as D ^F A. staff-note: one note in ABC with its octave, such as G, ^F or c. keyboard: one ABC note (C, ^F, _B, c). algebra-tiles: the two sides multiplied, such as (x + 2)(x + 3). clock: a time H:MM with an hour from 1 to 12, such as 3:45. measure: the size of the angle, a number.

accepted_answers.description: fill-in-blank, numeric, expression, keyboard, algebra-tiles, clock, measure: other answers that count as right.

form.description: algebra-tiles only: the form the answer must take; product (two sides multiplied) is the one form.

step_minutes.description: clock only: how far one step of the minute hand goes (default 5); divides 60.

tolerance.description: numeric, measure only: how far off an answer may be (absolute), e.g. 0.01 for two decimals or 2 for a protractor reading.

unit.description: numeric, measure only: shown after the answer box; the learner may type it or not.

tool.description: measure only: the tool drawn to measure with.

angle.description: measure only: the angle drawn, in degrees.

abc.description:
Music in ABC notation, drawn as a staff above the prompt, e.g. "X:1
L:1/4
K:C
A" for one note. fill-bar: the bar, with one invisible rest (x2) marking the gap.

tiles.description: fill-bar: note values in ABC (B2, BB, B/B/B), one group per tile without spaces; a tile may be used more than once. algebra-tiles: the pile as a x^2 + b x + c with whole a from 1 to 3, b from 0 to 12, c from 0 to 20, such as x^2 + 5x + 6. chord-spell: the notes to pick from in ABC, as one string separated by spaces (D E F ^F _G A B) or a list; every note of the answer and at least one more.

exact.description: fill-bar only: only correct_answer (and accepted_answers) count, instead of any tiles that fill the gap.

play.description:
Music in ABC notation that a speaker button plays (Web Audio tones), e.g. "X:1
L:1/2
K:C
C G". Two single notes play one after the other, then together. Without abc, the notes are drawn on a staff once the question is answered.

option_kind.description: multiple-choice with play or abc: abc draws each option as a staff (its notes after the header of play, else abc).

clef.description: staff-note only: the staff the learner places the note on.

any_octave.description: staff-note only: the note counts in any octave.

octave.description: keyboard only: only the exact key counts, not the same note in another octave.

octaves.description: keyboard only: how many octaves of keys, from middle C.

set.description: A paradigm set key from the manifest.

forms.description: One entry per paradigm slot key.

listening_item.description: A sentence for listening practice: read aloud by the browser, typed by the learner.

text.description: The sentence exactly as it should be typed (1 to 30 words).

note.description: Optional pointer: the grammar at work, or 'New word: <word> = <meaning>.'

play.description: A speaker tile: music in ABC notation, played on a tap, in place of text.

abc.description: A tune in ABC notation with one wrong note, drawn as a staff in place of the sentence (#1227).

wrong.description: Must appear exactly once in sentence; with abc, the wrong note's number, counting from 1.

fix.description: What the wrong word should have been; with abc, one note in ABC (F, ^C, _B).

items.description: A spot has a sentence or abc, not both.

scales.description: Build the scale (#1229): Sprint mode's ladder with notes. The first rung is filled; the learner taps the other seven from the scale's notes and the decoys.

notes.description: Eight ABC notes separated by spaces, bottom to top: "D E ^F G A B ^c d".

decoys.description: ABC notes separated by spaces that are not in the scale, mixed into the bank: "F c". The octave doesn't count: c is C.

placement.title: placement.json
placement.description: The course's placement test (#1106), one per course, for a course with "levels": multiple-choice questions, each about one unit. A unit with written questions uses them; every other unit draws random_per_unit of its lessons' multiple-choice questions.

random_per_unit.description: For each unit without written questions: how many of its lessons' multiple-choice questions to draw at random.

unit.description: A unit id from the manifest.
A unit id from the manifest.

content.description: Markdown; each '## ' heading starts a card. A fenced block marked abc is music notation (ABC text), drawn as a staff.
